operation.summary: Send the owner a notice, a question (buttons, text reply, choice, links), an HTML card or a live text panel. Default to a styled HTML card (kind html, from GET /v1/samples, e.g. html-yes-no) for every test, yes/no, choice, notice or form; a native question or notice is the fallback. Normal priority and no speech. Sending isn't seeing or answering: wait with GET /v1/interactions/{id}?wait=55 (or one /v1/events loop for several)

body.name: kind
body.description: notice (one-way), question, html (a card you draw; answer comes from Bridgit.respond), pieces (a card the phone draws from pieces and sources; no HTML) or text (a live text panel you stream into with /v1/text/stream)

body.name: pieces
body.description: kind=pieces: 1-24 pieces (header, status, text, note, metrics, table, timeline, gallery, video, people, devices, draft, buttons), values as {"$source":"<source>.<path>"}. See https://bridgit.cc/learn/builder/applet-packages.md

body.name: sources
body.description: kind=pieces: up to 8 named sources: {"watch":"<your watch id>","read":"tally"|"status"} or {"call":{"path":"/v1/...","query":{}},"every_s":60-3600} (GET only)

body.name: fresh_s
body.description: kind=pieces: 30-86400; older data shows the card as stale

body.name: states
body.description: kind=pieces: your own words for the card states empty, loading, stale, paused, error

body.name: title
body.description: Up to 80 characters

body.name: text
body.description: Up to 2,000 characters

body.name: image
body.description: {"gallery_id"} or {"data_base64"}, up to 2 MB

body.name: html
body.description: kind=html: the card's HTML, up to 256 KB. Runs offline: no network, only data:image/* images; call Bridgit.respond(value) once per question view (up to 16 KB) to answer; value is a JSON string or a plain object/array, which is serialized for you. window.Bridget is the same object (the only name on 1.6.269 and older). After persistence, bridgit:answered lets the card show its confirmation; the trusted Back to questions control reloads the question for resubmission. Bridgit.act({method, path, query?, body?}) runs one of your own endpoints on the phone right away, as you, with your grants and the owner's switches, e.g. await Bridgit.act({path:'/v1/flashlight', body:{on:true, auto_off_seconds:1}}) resolves to {ok, status, body}. A request is at most 16 KB (bigger: error request_too_big, so send a capture_id or gallery_id, never photo bytes) and a JSON reply over 64 KB comes back ok: false, error reply_too_big with the fix (ask for less). You get an action.executed event for each call, so it works while you're offline. A single card can't be swiped: show progress as text ("Step 2 of 5"), not swipe or segment bars. Complete pages: GET /v1/samples. A card app that decides or watches (Jev for text, Clef for photos and sound, POST /v1/watches with the free camera change check): https://bridgit.cc/learn/decisions.md

body.name: controls
body.description: Question: 1-6 of {type: button|text|choice|link, id, label, style?, placeholder?, options?, url?, package?}. Notice: links only

body.name: priority
body.description: normal or urgent

body.name: speak
body.description: Read it aloud on the phone

body.name: no_takeover
body.description: No takeover: true delivers this interaction to the Inbox and notifications without opening it, even while Bridgit is in front. Default false: opens automatically, subject to the owner setting and Android Display over other apps permission

body.name: follow_up
body.description: Card flows: true when you will post another card once the owner answers or closes this one. The card screen says "Waiting for the next card…" and stays up to 30 s; your next card replaces it in place, and Bridgit steps back to what the owner was doing only after the last card of the flow. Post the next card as soon as the answer or dismissed event arrives; leave it out (or false) on the last card. If the owner answered from the notification without the card on screen, nothing is held and the next card opens as usual. Ignored with no_takeover

body.name: expires_in_seconds
body.description: 60 to 604800, default 86400. After it, waits return expired and you get interaction.expired, but a question stays on the owner's phone and they can still answer it late (interaction.answered with late=true)

body.name: stack
body.description: kind=html: 1-32 letters, digits, - or _. Your cards with the same stack id form one stack the owner swipes through (drag left = next, right = previous) with "n of m" and a peek of the next card; each card keeps its own id, wait and answer. Up to 10 cards per stack id; an open stack counts as one of your 5 open questions. Leave it out for a single card, which is never swipeable. Don't rely on horizontal scrolling inside a stacked card. Wait on GET /v1/events?types=interaction.answered rather than one wait per card

body.name: stack_index
body.description: kind=html with stack: position 0-9 (default: after the cards already posted)

body.name: swipe_answer
body.description: kind=html with stack: {"left": label, "right": label} (1-20 characters each). While the card waits, a swipe answers it and moves on: answer.data = {"swipe": "left"|"right", "label": ...}. Bridgit shows both labels under the card

body.name: presentation
body.description: standard (default: inside Bridgit's bordered card box, with the toolbar and the status/Dismiss strip) or full_screen (kind html only: edge to edge, system bars, toolbar and strip hidden; a tap on the screen edge or Back shows Dismiss and Exit full screen for a few seconds). A full-screen page without width=device-width in its viewport meta is scaled down to fit whole, letterboxed in black, never cropped. Compose full-screen pictures to display.viewport (or GET /v1/device/display full_screen_card; static specs are also at GET <team backend>/v1/names/{name}/specs) and show them with object-fit: contain. Other values: invalid_parameter

body.name: content_aspect
body.description: kind=html: the page's fixed shape as width:height, e.g. "16:9" or "1280x720". When it differs from the canvas by more than 10 %, the reply's display.aspect_mismatch says so (also checked from width/height in the page's viewport meta)

operation.returns: interaction_id, status, expires_at, display {shown_as: full_screen|bridgit_open|notification, full_screen (Bridgit came to the front over other apps; it says nothing about the card's layout, which is presentation), missing?: [open_on_arrival, display_over_other_apps], fix?, presentation (standard|full_screen), viewport {width_px, height_px, width_dp, height_dp, density} (the exact canvas the card's page gets in that presentation), aspect_mismatch? {content, viewport, advice} (the page's declared shape differs from the canvas by more than 10 %)}. When full_screen is false and missing is set, only a notification was shown; pass fix on to the owner. no_takeover=true returns notification without missing or fix. ignored? {field: why}: request fields Bridgit did not use (display is reply-only; ask for an edge-to-edge card with presentation)
